h1: The 7 Best Lawn Mowers Under $1000 of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Lawn Mowers Under $1000: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: the 7 best lawn mowers under $1000 in 2026, covering cordless, gas, corded and reel mowers for every yard size.
summary: The EGO Power+ LM2134SP-2 is our best overall for medium and larger lawns thanks to its 21 inch deck and self-propelled drive. The Greenworks 80V self-propelled gives the same format for less, the EGO LM2114 is the full-width push choice, and the PowerSmart EasyGlide is the gas option. For small yards, the Greenworks 16 inch and American reel mower fit.
intro: A budget of $1000 is far more than any of these mowers need, and that is the first thing to understand. The price jump from an ordinary 21 inch push mower to a self-propelled model with a bigger battery is a few hundred dollars, and the real decision is lawn size and slope, not how much you can spend. Most people overbuy power and underbuy the right deck width.

We reviewed seven mowers across cordless, gas, corded and manual reel types and ranked them on paper by deck width, drive type, power source and price tier. The ranking uses spec sheets and owner reports rather than cutting trials; every rank is set by what the pick gives up or gains compared with the mowers around it.

products.name: EGO Power+ 21-Inch Cordless Self-Propelled Mower LM2134SP-2
products.verdict: A full-size cordless mower with self-propelled drive on a broad battery platform.
products.description:
The EGO LM2134SP-2 has a 21 inch deck, a cordless battery platform and a self-propelled drive. It sits in the $500 and up tier, still well under the $1000 ceiling.

It ranks first because self-propelled drive removes most of the effort on a medium or large lawn, and the EGO platform is well established. The Greenworks 80V gives similar format for less, but this is the more premium choice.

It suits lawns of medium to large size. The caveat is that it costs the most of the cordless picks.
products.idealFor: Medium to large lawns where drive assistance matters.
products.skipIf: You have a small flat yard.

products.name: Greenworks 80V 21-Inch Self-Propelled Mower
products.verdict: Self-propel and a 21 inch deck without paying near the top price.
products.description:
The Greenworks 80V has a 21 inch deck, a self-propelled drive and an 80V 4Ah battery with a charger included. Spending runs in the $200-500 range.

It ranks second because it matches the EGO's format at a lower tier, but its battery platform is the less flexible of the two.

It suits buyers who want self-propel on a budget. The caveat is that the 4Ah battery limits runtime on larger lawns.
products.idealFor: Buyers wanting self-propel without top pricing.
products.skipIf: You have a very large lawn.

products.name: EGO Power+ LM2114 21-Inch Cordless Push Mower
products.verdict: A full-width EGO deck without the self-propel premium.
products.description:
The EGO LM2114 has a 21 inch deck on the 56V battery platform, with a battery and charger included. Spending runs in the $200-500 range.

It ranks third because a full-width deck matters more than drive on a standard lawn, but you push it yourself. The Greenworks 80V adds self-propel at a similar tier.

It suits standard-size lawns on flat ground. The caveat is that you do the pushing.
products.skipIf: Your lawn has slopes or is large.

products.name: PowerSmart EasyGlide 21-Inch Gas Mower
products.verdict: Gas runtime without any battery to manage.
products.description:
The PowerSmart EasyGlide has a 21 inch deck, a 144cc 4-stroke OHV engine and 3-in-1 mulch, bag and side discharge. Spending runs in the $200-500 range.

It ranks fourth because gas gives unlimited runtime but adds fuel, oil and maintenance. The cordless picks above are quieter and simpler.

It suits buyers who dislike battery charging. The caveat is routine gas engine upkeep.

products.name: Greenworks 40V 16-Inch Push Mower
products.verdict: A light, easy-to-store cordless mower for small yards.
products.description:
The Greenworks 40V has a 16 inch deck, a 40V 4Ah battery and charger included and 160Wh of included energy. Spending runs in the $200-500 range.

It ranks fifth because the narrower 16 inch deck means more passes than a 21 inch model. Its advantage is light weight and easy storage.

It suits small lawns and tight storage. The caveat is a smaller cutting width.
products.idealFor: Small lawns and tight storage spaces.
products.skipIf: You have a medium or large lawn.

products.name: American Lawn Mower 1204-14 14-Inch 4-Blade Push Reel Mower
products.verdict: No motor, battery or fuel, just a manual reel for small flat lawns.
products.description:
The American Lawn Mower 1204-14 has a 14 inch cutting width and a 4-blade manual reel with no motor, battery or fuel. Think of it as a $50-100 purchase.

It ranks sixth because it only works on small, flat, regularly mowed lawns, and tall or thick grass is a struggle. It wins on zero running cost.

It suits small, tidy lawns. The caveat is manual effort and a narrow deck.
products.skipIf: Your grass gets tall between cuts.

products.name: LawnMaster MEB1114K 15-Inch Corded Mower
products.verdict: A cheap corded mower with no battery to replace.
products.description:
The LawnMaster MEB1114K has a 15 inch deck and an 11-amp corded motor, with no battery to replace. Cost-wise it belongs to the $100-200 group.

It ranks last because the cord limits range and gets in the way around obstacles. Its advantage is no battery cost or charging.

It suits small, unobstructed yards close to an outlet. The caveat is the cord management.
products.idealFor: Small unobstructed yards near an outlet.
products.skipIf: Your yard has trees, beds or distance.

whatMatters.detail: Deck width is how wide a strip the blade cuts, and a wider deck means fewer passes. A 21 inch deck suits most medium yards, while 14 to 16 inches suits small lawns and tight storage. Measure your lawn roughly before choosing.
Self-propelled drive powers the wheels so you only steer, which matters on slopes and large lawns. It adds cost and weight. If your yard is flat and small, a push mower is enough.
Volts describe power platform and amp hours describe runtime. A 4Ah battery in a 21 inch mower runs a smaller lawn per charge. Check the battery size and whether a second battery is sold.
Gas mowers need fuel, oil changes and spark plug care. They run until the tank empties. If you dislike maintenance, a cordless model is simpler.
Corded mowers are cheap but limited by cord length and obstacles. Reel mowers are quiet and fuel free but struggle with tall grass. Be honest about your yard shape and grass height.

howToChoose.intro: Lawn size is the clearest guide to deck width and drive.

cards.label: Cordless
cards.text: Quiet, no fuel and minimal upkeep, with runtime set by battery size. Picks here: the EGO LM2134SP-2, EGO LM2114, Greenworks 80V and Greenworks 40V.

cards.label: Gas
cards.text: Unlimited runtime with a refill but needs fuel and engine care. Pick here: the PowerSmart EasyGlide.

howToChoose.note: Most buyers should default to cordless unless the lawn is very large.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A 16 to 21 inch deck, an included battery and charger and a body light enough to store in a garage corner.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The Greenworks 40V 16-Inch includes battery and charger and is light to store, while the EGO LM2114 offers a full 21 inch deck.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: Your lawn is large or sloped, where the EGO LM2134SP-2 with self-propel saves real effort.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Your lawn is small and flat, where the American reel mower or LawnMaster handles it for far less.

faq.q: Is $1000 too much for a lawn mower?
faq.a: Yes for most yards. Every mower here costs well under that. Buy for lawn size and terrain rather than budget.

faq.q: What is the biggest mower buying mistake?
faq.a: Choosing the wrong deck width. A narrow deck on a big lawn means endless passes. Match width to the area.

faq.q: Is self-propelled worth it over a push mower?
faq.a: On slopes or larger lawns, yes. On a small flat yard, a push mower saves money and weight. Consider your own effort.

faq.q: How do I set up a cordless mower?
faq.a: Charge the battery fully, fit it into the mower and set the cutting height. Fold the handle into place. Read the manual for safety latches.

faq.q: How do I maintain a lawn mower?
faq.a: Clean the deck after use, sharpen or replace blades yearly and charge batteries correctly. Gas mowers need oil and plug care. Store it dry.

faq.q: Can a reel mower handle my lawn?
faq.a: Only if the lawn is small, flat and mowed often. Tall or thick grass jams a reel. Choose a motorized mower otherwise.

finalTake: The EGO Power+ LM2134SP-2 is the best lawn mower under $1000 for medium and larger lawns because it combines a 21 inch deck with self-propelled drive. The Greenworks 80V gives similar format for less, and the EGO LM2114 is the full-width push pick. For small yards, the Greenworks 16 inch or American reel mower is plenty.
